newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. envoy meets Moussa in Cairo for Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy meets Moussa in Cairo for Hebron talks.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross met Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa in Cairo on Monday for talks officials said would include his attempts to mediate an Israeli-Palestinian agreement on the West Bank town of Hebron.

Ross arrived in the Egyptian capital from Israel, where Palestinian officials reported earlier in the day unexpected progress in the talks on an Israeli redeployment in the town and said Ross was trying to close a deal in time for Christmas.
A PLO official said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu joined the Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on Monday to try to bring them to a conclusion.
Two Palestinian negotiators, Hassan Asfour and Marwan Kanafani, briefed Moussa in Cairo before he met Ross. They did not speak to reporters.
Speaking to parliament on Monday, Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri urged the Israeli government to come to its senses and carry out its agreements with the Palestinians.
He said Israel would eventually be the prime beneficiary from Middle East peace.

"Today we call on the Israeli government to return to the right way, come to its senses, and go back to implementing the agreements made with the Palestinian Authority under the auspices of the international community," he said.
"When peace prevails and development prospers, Israel will learn that this is in its interests first and foremost."
In the West Bank, Palestinian security official Jibril Rajoub said he hoped a deal could be clinched on Monday.

Palestinian officials said there was agreement on some major disputed points, but other issues were left to be resolved in a meeting yet to be arranged between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

The U.S. envoy arrived in the Middle East on Saturday saying he hoped to reactivate talks. But he had played down hopes of a breakthrough, saying only that he expected to report to President Bill Clinton after a couple of days.
